tagline: Down Hope Street under the trees, on the parade route.
intro: From the Warren line Hope Street climbs Half-Mile Hill, drops to the marshes at the mouth of Silver Creek and rises again into downtown Bristol, under a canopy of mature trees for nearly the whole five miles. It follows the trade route of 1681 between Boston and Newport, whose last leg was a ferry from Bristol Point.

Downtown keeps a grid laid out in 1680 around the oldest common in Rhode Island, and nearly every cross street ends in a view of the harbor and Poppasquash Point. South of town the road narrows along Walker Cove, becomes Ferry Road and rises toward the Mount Hope Bridge, its deck 135 feet over Mount Hope Bay at the highest point.

moments.title: Colt State Park
moments.text: At the main gate on Hope Street two bronze bulls, Conrad and Pomeroy, stand guard over Samuel P. Colt's old farm under the inscription "Private Property, Public Welcome."

moments.title: Hope Street
moments.text: Bristol has kept the Fourth since 1785, and a 1995 federal highway amendment let it swap the white center lines on its parade route for red, white and blue.

moments.title: Ferry Road
moments.text: The town's stewardship plan counted 75 European lindens in a nearly unbroken allée over a third of a mile, left by the gardening summer people of the late 1800s.
